criterion: ROADMAP.md M3 criterion 1 (amended 2026-10-10): the material gallery's spheres, raw-hero and raw-hall render with GPU verdict verified at committed tolerances, and the rasterised frame's error against a path-traced reference is recorded per scene with its bound stated first. Third step after evidence/m3-ao-bvh-bounds.json and evidence/m3-gpu-ao-bvh-bounds.json; approved by the coordinator on 2026-10-17.
written: 2026-10-18, before the converter exists and before any run of what follows
adapters: WARP (D3D12, windows-latest) and lavapipe (Vulkan, ubuntu-24.04) in CI. No hardware GPU.

scenes.raw-hero: raw_native_cli --model raw-hero.gltf (the asset in the built-in test scene, as a loaded model is placed), the test scene's camera and light, 512 x 320, ray-traced AO on, --threads 4
scenes.raw-hall-nave: new --owned-scene raw-hall-nave: raw::owned::hallScene(hall()) (the nave camera at eye height down the arcade, its sun), 512 x 320, ray-traced AO on, --threads 4
scenes.control-sphere: new --owned-scene control-sphere: one UV sphere (radius 1, 64 x 48 quads, albedo 0.6) and nothing else, the test scene's light, 256 x 160. Convex and alone, so the raster's ambient-times-AO and unshadowed sun are exact there: it checks the converter's units, not the raster model

v1_hero.bound: GPU certificate verdict verified with rt true at the committed tolerances (raw/cert/gpu_tolerance.hpp), on both adapters
v1_hero.prediction: holds; raw-hero already verified at 320 x 200 on both (evidence/m3-gpu-ao-bvh-runs.json)

v2_hall.prediction: holds, moderate confidence: the compute raster mirrors the CPU raster's arithmetic; the RHI v3 G-buffer miss on the hall's flute slivers (evidence/m3-rhi3-runs.json) is a different pipeline

v3_gallery.what: raw_native_cli material-gallery --size 256 --spp 2: the GPU shading pass (pbr_shade) against the float64 reference, in exposed units
v3_gallery.bound: rmse_exposed at most 5e-4 and max_abs_exposed at most 0.05, on both adapters. This is what a pass means for the gallery: the same picture from the same lighting samples within these limits (the 512 px WARP run of 2026-10-12 gave 5.6e-5 and 0.029)

path_traced_error.converter: rt::ptFromScene (new): the raster scene's triangles, normals and albedos to a PtScene. Each mesh gets a 1 x 1 texture holding its albedo rounded to 8 bits and a pure Lambert material (specular 0, metallic 0). The raster lights a pixel with albedo x (0.2 + li max(0, n.l)) x AO (src/renderer/composite.cpp), so the path tracer gets a constant sky of radiance 0.2 (irradiance 0.2 pi on an open surface, giving 0.2 x albedo through Lambert) and a sun of irradiance pi x li in the light's direction. Camera: the raster's eye, centre, up and vertical field of view; both use the same pinhole convention.
path_traced_error.reference: pathTraceCpu, 128 samples a pixel, 8 bounces, seed 1, no jitter (the pixel centre, as the raster samples), Russian roulette as default, --threads 4. A second run with 1 bounce (direct sun and sky with visibility, no interreflection) is recorded to split the error, not judged.
path_traced_error.measure: Over pixels that both cover (the raster's mask.pgm and the path tracer's triangle AOV): luminance Y = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B of the GPU frame's HDR output (frame_hdr.pfm) and of the path-traced radiance. Relative RMSE = sqrt(mean((Yr - Yp)^2)) / mean(Yp); bias = mean(Yr - Yp) / mean(Yp); noise floor = sqrt(mean(variance AOV)) / mean(Yp), the path tracer's own standard error; coverage agreement = the fraction of all pixels where the two coverages agree.

p0_alignment.bound: coverage agreement at least 99% on every scene
p0_alignment.prediction: above 99.5%: the same triangles and the same camera; the disagreement is silhouette pixels

p1_control.bound: control-sphere: relative RMSE at most 0.02 + 3 x the noise floor, |bias| at most 0.02
p1_control.prediction: holds; the residue is the 8-bit albedo and the shading-normal terminator

p1b_false_control.bound: the converter with the sun's pi left out must fail p1 (relative RMSE above 0.1)

p2_hero.prediction: 0.2 to 0.45 with a positive bias: the raster has no sun shadow (the hero's shadow on the ground and on itself) and no interreflection, so it is brighter in shadow and darker in creases

p3_hall.prediction: 0.6 to 1.5 with a large positive bias: inside the hall the raster's ambient sees the sky wherever no geometry lies within the 2 m AO radius, and its sun is unshadowed, while the path tracer lets light in only through the atrium and the openings

p4_gallery.why: the path tracer v2 has a sun and a constant sky, not the gallery's three physical lights and procedural sky, and its material is metal-roughness GGX, not five of the gallery's seven families (clearcoat, sheen, anisotropy, iridescence, transmission). A path-traced gallery needs both added to the tracer; that is outside this step and is recorded as an open item.

does_not_prove: That the raster model is physically right (the error records how far it is from light transport, which is the point); anything on a hardware GPU; path-traced error for the gallery.
